title: Control plane version coordinator and shadow validation playbook for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Implement a version coordinator service and a shadow-traffic validation playbook to automate safe control-plane version promotions for Redwood Private (VPC) customers. The coordinator will integrate with existing Terraform IaC modules to stage changes, trigger canaries that shadow traffic for new control-plane agents, run deterministic health/assertion checks, collect metrics, and decide promote/rollback based on configurable gates. This ticket covers design, Terraform module extension, canary execution harness, health assertions, Prometheus/Tracing wiring, and a runbook for on-call engineers.
acceptance_criteria: A coordinator service exists that can schedule a staged upgrade window and annotate target tenant groups in the control plane
Terraform modules include a 'canary' flag and version variables that can be toggled without full re-apply for a staged promotion
Shadow canary path mirrors production control plane traffic for a configurable cohort and does not mutate customer state
Automated health assertions run after shadowing: API conformance, lease reconciliations, operator heartbeats, DB migration harmonics
A promotion decision is produced (promote/hold/rollback) within the configured SLO (default 30 minutes) and logged to audit streams
Playbook documented with clear rollback steps, expected metrics, and escalation path; security review completed and approved
implementation_steps: Design coordinator state machine (staged -> shadowing -> evaluation -> promote/rollback)
Extend Terraform private modules: add 'version_coordinator' module, expose per-tenant 'upgrade_cohort' tag and 'shadow_listener' param
Implement shadow proxy that duplicates inbound control-plane requests to canary agents with header 'X-Shadow-Only'
Create health assertion library (python/golang) to run a suite of non-destructive checks against canary agents
Wire metrics and traces: add span attributes 'upgrade.cohort' and canary_tags; create Grafana dashboard and kube-prometheus alerts
Implement coordinator API to orchestrate cohorts, schedule windows, and post decisions to audit-log (CloudWatch/BigQuery)
terraform_changes: modules/controlplane/main.tf accepts 'upgrade_cohort' label and creates a canary nodepool when present
State migration: ensure nodepool naming scheme supports rollback without conflicting resource names
Provide example overlay in examples/private-upgrade/ to demonstrate canary toggles and rollout variables
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Dry run: coordinator schedules a window; shadow proxy duplicates 0% traffic to canaries; run assertion suite against synthetic traffic
Stage 1 - Shadow small cohort: route 1% of mirrored traffic from low-risk tenants for 2 hours; baseline metrics collected
Stage 2 - Expanded shadow: increase to 10% mirrored traffic across heterogeneous tenants, run destructive-safety gates disabled
Stage 3 - Canary promotion: if gates pass, promote cohort to live (traffic slicing with incremental cutover) or roll back if failures detected
Stage 4 - Post-promotion monitoring: 24h intensified telemetry; automatic rollback window open for 2h if critical SLOs breach
health_checks: API conformance: endpoint schema checks and sample interaction flows run against canary agents
KV cache consistency: verify that KV reads/writes for ephemeral keys behave identically in shadowed flows
Operator heartbeats: check that reconciliation loop latencies remain within 2x baseline
Database migrations harmonics: ensure migrations are idempotent and check row counts and schema versions
Latency percentile gates: p50/p95/p99 for core control-plane RPCs compared to baseline cohort with tolerance thresholds
Error budget checks: ensure error rate increase does not exceed 0.5% absolute for 30m window
telemetry_and_alerts: Create Grafana: 'Upgrade Coordinator' dashboard with cohort-level metrics, diffs vs baseline, and top-10 traces
Audit logs: coordinator decisions (promote/hold/rollback) written to central audit topic with request IDs
Synthetic verification: scheduled smoke tests and end-to-end checks fired during every staged window
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shadowing accidentally mutates tenant state. Mitigation: proxy enforces X-Shadow-Only and rejects state-changing ops, all DB writes routed to a sandbox during shadowing
Risk: Terraform state drift when creating/removing canary nodepools. Mitigation: adopt immutable naming patterns and a short-lived canary pool lifecycle with tags
Risk: Insufficient telemetry for small cohorts. Mitigation: increase sampling / instrument higher-fidelity traces during canaries
Risk: Coordinator becomes single point of failure. Mitigation: coordinator is implemented as leader-election pair with read-only observers; decisions are idempotent and stored in durable audit logs
testing_plan: Unit tests for coordinator state transitions and decision logic
Integration tests: terraform apply in a staging VPC that creates a canary nodepool and runs the shadow proxy
Chaos tests: simulate increased latency and DB errors during shadowing to validate automatic rollback
Load test: synthetic traffic generator to validate p99 behavior for canary agents at expected load profiles
runbook: If an automatic 'rollback' decision is triggered, coordinator will start graceful drain of canary agents and re-route traffic to previous version
On-call steps: verify alert details, check coordinator audit logs, review Grafana cohort diffs, and if needed open an incident and trigger manual rollback
Manual rollback: run terraform apply with previous 'version' variable and scale down canary nodepool after verification
Post-incident: run retrospective, capture root cause, and add new assertions to health-check suite
